conviction_note: The stock is already down about 55% since the July print on two disclosed hits: cost trouble flagged by management on 15 Sep, and the 3.5-star rating on H3815 on 8 Oct. The open question is how big the Q3 medical-cost miss is and whether full-year adjusted EBITDA ($145-163m) gets cut. TD Cowen's $16m cut to second-half EBITDA puts the Street near or below the low end already. Against that: peers' Q3 MA results were benign, 12.9% of float is short, and consensus is a loss. The findings sum to -0.9. The scaled number is (2*0.46-1)*11 = -0.88. Both are small because the bad news is largely public and the name's reaction history (2 of 7 up, last four down) tilts the sign only slightly.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue guide $1.300-1.320bn; adj. gross profit $148-158m; adj. EBITDA $20-30m; membership 295.5-297.5k. FY26 guide: revenue $5.195-5.225bn, adj. EBITDA $145-163m, membership 298-301k (company 8-K exhibit 99.1, 2026-07-30, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001832466/000117184326005078/exh_991.htm). Consensus Q3 EPS: -$0.04 per finviz (https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=ALHC, read 2026-10-29) and Earnings Whispers (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/ALHC/21162, 2026-10-21), with revenue about $1.31bn. Chartmill has -$0.03 and Benzinga +$0.03, so EPS is two-source agreeing but disputed at the edges. EBITDA guide is the company's own. H1 adj. EBITDA was $37.9m + $68.1m = $106.0m, so the FY guide implies H2 $39-57m and Q4 about $19-27m. The trade turns on adj. MBR / EBITDA versus guide and on the FY EBITDA guide.
positioning_check: Short float 12.86%, short ratio (days to cover) 3.1, 25.52m shares short (finviz, https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=ALHC, read 2026-10-29 13:22 ET). Moderate, not crowded. The baseline has 25d skew null (unavailable). Put/call open-interest ratio is 0.05: open interest is overwhelmingly calls. ATM spread is 53% of mid, so the 7.72% event-implied move is indicative only. Spot $8.235 is -66.5% from the 52-week high and +9.2% off the low. 20d run-up is +6.4%, 5d is -2.3%. Analyst stance: William Blair downgraded to Market Perform 2026-10-09. JPM and KeyBanc cut targets to $10/$12 but kept Overweight. TD Cowen cut its target to $12 and kept Buy. findings.finding: Management disclosed on 15 Sep (Baird conference) rising hospital and skilled-nursing costs, partly 2025 hospital bills lagging through a claims-system transition. On 9 Oct William Blair downgraded and said it expects Q3 to show cost-trend problems. TD Cowen cut its H2 adj. EBITDA by about $16m on inpatient utilization. That cut takes implied FY EBITDA to roughly $139-141m against the company's $145-163m guide (H2 guide $39-57m). The release is the first quantification: Q3 adj. MBR against the $148-158m adj. gross profit guide, any unfavorable prior-year development (Q2 already carried about $6m), and whether FY EBITDA is cut.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July print (Q2 beat, Q3 EBITDA guide soft) fell -20.2%. The 15 Sep conference remarks on costs cost -16% in a session (OCBJ). The April print fell -10.1%. This name has sold guidance and cost disappointments hard, every time over the last four prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the stock is -55% since July and the sell-side has cut. What is not priced is the size. No number has been given for the cost overrun or the reserve hit, and if the FY guide were already cut by the company the Street would not be split between -$0.04 and +$0.03. If fully priced, the stock would not have bounced to $8.2 from the $7.5 low, and Cowen would not still say the pressure does not extend into 2027.
findings.independence: Separate sources point the same way. TD Cowen's H2 EBITDA cut on inpatient utilization (https://www.webull.com/news/15736444743656448, 2026-10-12). William Blair's Q3 cost-trend warning (https://www.tikr.com/blog/alignment-healthcare-sinks-20-as-medicare-plan-downgraded-humana-and-clover-soar, 2026-10-09). The Earnings Whispers preview noting the Q2 unfavorable reserve adjustment (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/ALHC/21162). All trace back to the same management disclosure.

findings.finding: The 2027 Star Ratings (released 8 Oct) cut California HMO contract H3815, about 75% of members, from 4.0 to 3.5. Per the company's own 8-K this removes quality bonus payments for FY2028 only, partly offset by provider risk-sharing, with no revenue impact in 2026 or 2027. The company is pursuing appeals and litigation (complaint filed 9 Oct). The call is the first chance to quantify the 2028 hit and the mitigation, and to say whether 2027 bids/benefits change.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the 8-K the stock was -19 to -20% premarket on 9 Oct but closed about -13.4%, then bounced +8.6% on 12 Oct (webull). It now trades about $8.2, above the post-ratings close, so the market has already partly looked through it.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. Targets were cut to $10-12 and the stock fell double digits. The unpriced residual is only the dollar size of the 2028 QBP loss net of risk-sharing, which the company has not given. A quantified number above or below the roughly 2-3 points of H3815 revenue the Street implicitly assumes could move the stock either way.
findings.independence: The TIKR article (https://www.tikr.com/blog/alignment-healthcare-sinks-20-as-medicare-plan-downgraded-humana-and-clover-soar) reports the same 8-K plus analyst reactions. One document, so one finding.

findings.finding: The large peers that reported Q3 2026 since ALHC last spoke all came in better than expected on medical costs. UnitedHealth's Q3 MCR was 88.4% against about 89.9% expected, including $610m of favorable 2026 prior-period development (13 Oct). Centene's MLR was 92.7% against 92.84% expected, helped by 'steadier Medicare Advantage results', with guidance raised. Elevance said MA performed better than expected. Industry-wide Q3 MA cost trend looks benign, which bounds how bad an idiosyncratic ALHC overrun is likely to be.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline record of ALHC trading on peer read-through. ALHC's own cost problem is described by management as company-specific (claims system), which limits transmission.
findings.why_not_priced: ALHC has not reacted to peers' beats: it is +6.4% over 20 days but -2.3% over 5 days through Elevance and Centene. The Street's ALHC consensus moved to a loss after these peer prints. If the read-through were priced, ALHC estimates would have firmed rather than been cut.
findings.independence: Centene Q3 beat with steadier MA (https://finimize.com/content/centene-lifted-its-2026-profit-outlook-after-a-big-q3-beat). Elevance MA better than expected (https://www.fiercehealthcare.com/payers/elevance-health-shares-rise-premarket-q3-earnings-revenue-beat). This is a proxy: no direct counterparty of ALHC has confirmed it.

findings.finding: The bar into the print is very low and the setup leans long: Q3 consensus is a loss of -$0.04 (vs +$0.02 a year ago), the stock is -66% from its high, 12.9% of float is short (3.1 days to cover), and the option open interest is 95% calls (put/call OI 0.05). Management pre-announced Q3 as a planned trough ($20-30m EBITDA on deliberate double-digit-million investment). An in-guide quarter with FY held would clear a bar the sell-side has already lowered.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last two upside reactions (+16.5% Feb 2025, +6.0% Jul 2025) came off depressed setups. The four most recent prints were all negative.
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown has a named cause, so this is not an unexplained-drawdown claim. The lowered bar is itself what the price reflects. If the market expected an in-guide print, the stock would not trade at 0.15x sales with analysts' targets at $10-12, and Needham would not have initiated at only Hold the day before.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview frames Q3 as a planned dip, -$0.04 consensus (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/ALHC/21162, 2026-10-21). It shares the consensus figure with finviz.

findings.finding: For 2027 Alignment expands to 77 plans in 55 counties across 5 states (from 45 counties), adding 10 counties with over 934k Medicare eligibles, including Charlotte NC and Kern/Kings/Tulare CA. It adds Hoag to the HMO network and Astrana Health. It is expanding while several carriers retrench. The call will give the first read on AEP 2027 and the roughly 20% growth goal.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 12 Oct plan-launch PR (Central Health Harmony) coincided with a +8.6% relief bounce. The baseline has no history of the stock trading on membership guides alone.
findings.why_not_priced: The footprint is public, but the membership and margin consequences are not: no 2027 membership or margin number has been given. A 2.5-star drop on the flagship contract could cost 2028 benefit competitiveness, so the market is not paying for 2027 growth. If priced, the stock would not trade on 2028 QBP fears alone.

outside_window.finding: Administrative appeal and federal litigation (complaint filed 2026-10-09) over H3815's 3.5-star 2027 rating. A win would restore FY2028 quality bonus payments, but no ruling is dated inside the window.
